## route-scope/status-not-declared
# a mapped error is answered as one of the operation's own responses
rejected: Controller.swift:11: error: @ErrorResponse(Gone.self, .notFound) on 'opA' maps to a status the document does not declare for it. It declares .ok. A mapped error is answered as one of the operation's own responses, so the document has to describe it — add it there, or map to one it already declares.

## route-scope/pair-form-against-a-bodied-response
# a bare case cannot construct a response the document gives a body
rejected: Controller.swift:11: error: @ErrorResponse(Gone.self, .notFound) on 'opA' maps to a 404 response that carries a body, so a status alone cannot construct it. Supply one — @ErrorResponse(Gone.self, .notFound, { e in … }).

## route-scope/closure-form-against-a-bare-response
# a response carrying nothing has nowhere to put a body
rejected: Controller.swift:11: error: @ErrorResponse(Gone.self, .notFound, …) on 'opA' supplies a body, but the document's 404 response carries none. Drop the closure.

## route-scope/terminal-scoped-pair-form-against-a-bodied-response
# a terminal-scoped mapping is exempt from naming a declared status, but not from the form of one the document does declare — it still gets a forwarder clause
rejected: Controller.swift:11: error: @ErrorResponse(DecodingError.self, .notFound) on 'opA' maps to a 404 response that carries a body, so a status alone cannot construct it. Supply one — @ErrorResponse(DecodingError.self, .notFound, { e in … }).

## route-scope/unconstructible-content-type
# the shim builds JSON bodies only
rejected: Controller.swift:11: error: @ErrorResponse(Gone.self, .notFound) on 'opA' maps to a 404 response whose content type this adapter cannot construct — it builds JSON bodies only. Use @RawOperation for this operation.

## controller-scope/status-not-declared-for-some-operations
# a controller mapping covers every operation, so every one has to declare the status
rejected: Controller.swift:9: error: @ErrorResponse(Gone.self, .notFound) on 'GateController' maps to a status the document does not declare for 'opB'. A mapped error is answered as one of the operation's own responses, so every operation the mapping covers has to declare 404 — add it there, or move the mapping to the operations that do.

## controller-scope/pair-form-against-a-bodied-response

rejected: Controller.swift:9: error: @ErrorResponse(Gone.self, .notFound) on 'GateController' maps to a 404 response that carries a body for 'opA', so a status alone cannot construct it. Supply one — @ErrorResponse(Gone.self, .notFound, { e in … }).

## controller-scope/closure-form-against-a-bare-response
# and in the other direction
rejected: Controller.swift:9: error: @ErrorResponse(Gone.self, .notFound, …) on 'GateController' supplies a body, but the document's 404 response carries none for 'opA'. Drop the closure.

## controller-scope/covered-operations-disagree-about-a-body
# the failure only controller scope can have: no form serves both, so the fix is to move the mapping rather than to change it
rejected: Controller.swift:9: error: @ErrorResponse(Gone.self, .notFound) on 'GateController' covers operations whose 404 responses disagree about carrying a body — with: 'opA'; without: 'opB'. One mapping cannot construct both — move it to route scope on each, or make the document agree.

## controller-scope/unconstructible-content-type
# reported before the pair/closure question, which has no right answer here

## ordering/catch-all-is-not-last
# a catch-all matches everything, so anything after it is dead
rejected: Controller.swift:12: error: @ErrorResponse(Swift.Error.self, .notFound) on 'opA' is a catch-all, so the mappings after it can never match — Gone. Put the catch-all last.

## parameters/assertion-on-a-type-the-format-changed
# `format: date-time` is emitted as a Foundation.Date, so a string assertion has nothing to measure — the value is not a string by the time a check could run
rejected: Controller.swift:10: error: 'query.q' in the request of 'opA' declares `minLength`, which this adapter cannot check because the generator emits `format: date-time` as a Foundation.Date, not a String. Remove it from the document, or check it in the handler. @RawOperation is not an escape — validation is emitted for those too, from the same document.

## parameters/pattern-swift-cannot-compile
# patterns are compiled at build time, so an unreadable one fails the build naming the parameter rather than trapping on the first request that reaches it
rejected: Controller.swift:10: error: 'query.q' in the request of 'opA' declares `pattern: [a-`, which Swift's regular-expression engine cannot compile. JSON Schema patterns are ECMA-262; most translate directly, but this one does not. Rewrite it, or remove it and check it in the handler.

rejected: Controller.swift:10: error: 'body' in the request of 'opA' declares `minProperties`, which this adapter cannot check because a generated struct has a fixed set of members and no runtime property count. Remove it from the document, or check it in the handler. @RawOperation is not an escape — validation is emitted for those too, from the same document.

## schemas/assertion-beneath-a-oneOf

## tuple/status-with-no-success
# with no documented success, no return shape helps; only the document can
rejected: Controller.swift:9: error: 'opA' returns a status enum, but documents no success response, so there is nothing to choose between. Document the successes it can answer with.

## tuple/status-beside-an-annotation
# a status returned and a status annotated contradict each other
rejected: Controller.swift:10: error: 'opA' returns a status enum and also names a status with @JSONResponse(status: .created). The two contradict each other — drop the annotation, or return without the status enum.

## tuple/successes-disagree-on-a-body
# the handler has one body to answer every success with, so all must agree on carrying one
rejected: Controller.swift:9: error: 'opA' returns a status enum with a body, but its documented 204 success carries none. Every success a status enum can answer with has to agree on whether it carries a body — document them alike, or use @RawOperation.

## tuple/not-a-response-shape
# the labels are read in WireMVC's canonical order, and anything else is not a response tuple
rejected: Controller.swift:9: error: the response tuple returned by @Operation 'opA' is labelled (body:status:), which is not a response shape — write (status:body:) or (headers:body:).

## tuple/status-is-an-http-response-status
# a WireMVC route's status type would let the handler return one the document does not declare
rejected: Controller.swift:9: error: 'opA' returns its status as 'HTTPResponse.Status', which would let the handler answer with a status its document does not declare. Return an enum of the documented successes instead. Declare `extension Operations.OpA { enum SuccessStatus: Sendable, Hashable { case ok(Operations.OpA.Output.Ok.Headers); case created(Operations.OpA.Output.Created.Headers) } }` and return `(status: Operations.OpA.SuccessStatus, body: String)`.

## tuple/status-enum-not-declared
# the cases are checked against the document, so the enum has to be one this build can read
rejected: Controller.swift:9: error: 'opA' returns its status as 'Operations.OpA.SuccessStatus', which names no enum declared in the sources this build reads. The status has to be an enum of the documented successes. Declare `extension Operations.OpA { enum SuccessStatus: Sendable, Hashable { case ok; case created } }` and return `(status: Operations.OpA.SuccessStatus, body: String)`.

## tuple/status-enum-cases-differ
# the enum is what the compiler holds the handler to, so it must be exactly the successes
rejected: Controller.swift:9: error: 'opA' returns its status as 'Operations.OpA.SuccessStatus', whose cases must be exactly the operation's documented successes (.ok, .created). It declares .accepted, which the document does not, and omits .created, which the document declares.

## tuple/http-fields-beside-a-status
# WireMVC's (status:headers:body:) is not an operation's shape: headers travel in the cases
rejected: Controller.swift:9: error: 'opA' returns header fields beside its status, but an operation's headers travel in its status enum: each case whose response declares headers carries them. Declare `extension Operations.OpA { enum SuccessStatus: Sendable, Hashable { case ok(Operations.OpA.Output.Ok.Headers); case created(Operations.OpA.Output.Created.Headers) } }` and return `(status: Operations.OpA.SuccessStatus, body: String)`.

## tuple/case-without-its-headers
# a headered response's case must carry its headers, or the response could not be built
rejected: Controller.swift:9: error: 'opA' returns its status as 'Operations.OpA.SuccessStatus', whose case .created carries no headers, but the documented 201 response declares the header 'Location'. Declare it as `case created(Operations.OpA.Output.Created.Headers)`.

## tuple/case-with-the-wrong-headers
# a case carries exactly its own response's headers, not another response's
rejected: Controller.swift:9: error: 'opA' returns its status as 'Operations.OpA.SuccessStatus', whose case .created carries (Operations.OpA.Output.Ok.Headers), but the documented 201 response's headers are `Operations.OpA.Output.Created.Headers`. Declare it as `case created(Operations.OpA.Output.Created.Headers)`.

## tuple/case-with-headers-its-response-lacks
# a response declaring no headers has no Headers type for its case to carry
rejected: Controller.swift:9: error: 'opA' returns its status as 'Operations.OpA.SuccessStatus', whose case .created carries a payload, but the documented 201 response declares no headers, so there is nothing for it to carry. Declare it as `case created`.

## tuple/headers-as-http-fields

## tuple/headers-of-another-response
